name: Radiant Thermal Lance RTL-8 'Hearthstone'
description:
The RTL-8 generates a narrow coherent beam of mid-infrared radiation tuned to the peak absorption frequency of water-bearing biological tissue — approximately 3 micrometers wavelength — delivered through a zinc selenide optical assembly housed in a matte ceramic barrel. Unlike visible-spectrum laser weapons that deposit energy on surface layers, the RTL-8's chosen wavelength penetrates 2–4 millimeters into tissue before converting to heat, cooking target structures from within while leaving the outermost dermal layer initially intact. The subjective experience for unprotected targets is described by medical examiners as 'subsurface thermal necrosis' — the tissue beneath the skin liquefies before the surface shows visible damage.

The RTL-8's power management system draws from a high-density thermal battery that doubles as a heat sink, with a passive radiator array along the weapon's spine that glows a deep amber during sustained operation — a distinctive visual signature that operators sometimes use deliberately as a psychological deterrent. The weapon operates in three modes: pulse (0.1-second burst, low thermal signature), sustained (continuous beam up to 4 seconds before mandatory cooldown), and 'cathedral' mode (maximum output, 1.8 seconds, visible steam or smoke from target, requires 40-second full cooldown).

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the RTL-8 under a medical research contract for non-invasive tissue ablation in surgical contexts, and the weapon's design philosophy still reflects that clinical origin. ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS purchased manufacturing rights after a field evaluation demonstrated its effectiveness against targets in thermal-insulated suits, which conventional laser weapons struggle to defeat. The name 'Hearthstone' emerged from field operators who noted that a weapon firing in cathedral mode warms everything in a 3-meter radius.
manufacturer: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS (design origin); ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (military production)
specifications: wavelength: 3.0 micrometers (mid-infrared) optical assembly: Zinc selenide focusing array penetration depth tissue: 2–4 mm beam modes: Pulse (0.1s) / Sustained (up to 4s) / Cathedral (1.8s max output) cathedral cooldown: 40 seconds battery capacity: 18 pulse shots / 6 sustained cycles / 3 cathedral shots effective range: Up to 40 m (optimal); degraded past 60 m weight: 2.7 kg length: 54 cm thermal bleed radius cathedral: ~3 m ambient warming
tactical_use: RTL-8 operators exploit its subsurface damage mechanism against targets in thermal armor, where conventional weapons struggle. Pulse mode is used for precision suppression at range with minimal collateral heat. Sustained mode handles material cutting — doors, sensor arrays, vehicle optics. Cathedral mode is reserved for hardened single targets or rapid material breaching when time is critical and cooldown is acceptable. The weapon's amber glow during operation is sometimes used deliberately to signal capability and force surrender without firing.
cultural_context: The RTL-8's medical origin gives it a disturbing dual identity in GLMZ. Surgeons and HELIX BIOSYSTEMS researchers recognize the design language immediately, which creates a specific kind of horror when the weapon appears in violent contexts. Among military operators it carries a reputation for being 'clean' in the bureaucratic sense — the damage profile is difficult to attribute to a specific weapon in autopsies, which makes it attractive for deniable operations. Street-level criminals rarely encounter it; its presence signals either military or high-tier corporate involvement.
known_users: High-tier bounty hunters specializing in armored targets
Black-market surgeons who've repurposed the medical variant
story_hooks: A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS whistleblower is found dead with RTL-8 tissue damage — but the weapon was supposed to be locked in a military-only supply chain, suggesting someone inside HELIX authorized its use.
The players acquire an RTL-8 with a HELIX medical serial number, not an ARCTURUS military one — tracing its provenance leads to a secret program that was officially cancelled.

An ARCTURUS operator using an RTL-8 in cathedral mode in a confined space has caused structural damage to a civilian habitat; the corporation wants the incident buried and hires the players to manage the aftermath.

A religious cult in GLMZ's lower districts has acquired an RTL-8 and incorporated it into ritual practice, calling it a 'divine light' — their leader knows exactly what it does and is using it for controlled killings disguised as miracles.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, purposeful energy weapon with a distinctly medical-industrial aesthetic — part surgical instrument, part thermal deterrent. The RTL-8 presents as a tapered rifle with a prominent barrel assembly and a pronounced heat-management spine running the length of the receiver. Its silhouette is angular but refined, suggesting precision engineering rather than brute-force lethality.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 54 cm | Barrel assembly: 18 cm | Grip-to-trigger guard: 12 cm | Width across radiator array: 6.5 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and surprisingly manageable at 2.7 kg — the thermal battery housing sits low in the stock, creating a stable center of gravity. Feels substantial without being unwieldy; the weight distribution favors forward control during sustained operation.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte ceramic barrel shroud (heat-resistant composite) with aerospace-grade aluminum alloy receiver frame. Zinc selenide optical assembly (visible as a subtle amber-tinted focusing lens at barrel terminus). Reinforced polymer furniture with integrated thermal venting.
physical_description.finish: Matte ceramic white-gray barrel exterior with brushed charcoal aluminum receiver. Satin-black grip and stock sections. High-contrast aesthetic suggests clinical precision over tactical anonymity.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte ceramic white and brushed charcoal gray | Accents: deep amber (zinc selenide lens), copper-bronze radiator fins | Glowing amber undertones during operation
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with subtle grip ridges for wet-environment handling. Textured control surfaces around mode-selector buttons. Cool to the touch until sustained operation begins.
distinctive_features: Prominent radiator spine with copper-bronze heat-dissipation fins running the full weapon length
Amber-tinted zinc selenide focusing lens at barrel terminus — faintly luminescent even in standby
Three discrete mode-selector buttons (pulse/sustained/cathedral) with tactile detents, marked with Φ currency symbols indicating restricted availability
Heat-bleed indicator ring around barrel mid-section that shifts from matte to glossy finish under thermal load
Dual exhaust vents along the sides of the receiver — sealed during normal operation, venting vapor during cathedral mode
Integrated passive radiator array that visibly glows deep amber during sustained cycles
Minimalist ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS plate inset into the stock, deliberately understated
Charging port recessed beneath the radiator spine — medical-grade connector suggesting original HELIX BIOSYSTEMS origin
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Stamped ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo (angular 'A' design) on the stock, positioned low and to the right. Smaller HELIX BIOSYSTEMS heritage mark laser-etched near the charging port — a subtle acknowledgment of surgical origins. Serial designation on the left side of the receiver in military alphanumeric format.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically observed well-maintained with minimal field wear on high-use examples — the ceramic barrel shows micro-stress fractures from repeated thermal cycling, appearing as fine spider-web patterns under close inspection. Radiator fins may display residual amber discoloration from repeated cycling. Professional operators keep the zinc selenide lens meticulously clean; neglected examples show faint amber haze from dust accumulation.
